scope: Preliminary TITLE.DLL symbol/data closure from implied link symbols of masked rows. Diagnostic only: it informs translation-unit and link-order hypotheses; it proves no layout and grants no acceptance.

findings.claim: Uninitialized data near 0x29570-0x2b360 is laid out in code order.
findings.evidence: 163 single-owner .bss addresses form 38 non-decreasing runs; the long runs follow code order across many functions (e.g. 0x2aa54-0x2af68 for code 0x10ce0-0x1beb0).
findings.interpretation: Consistent with per-object .bss contributions in link order (static or C++ globals).

findings.claim: From about 0x2b370, uninitialized data is shared across units and out of code order.
findings.evidence: g_engine_interface (0x2bb40, 150 referencing rows), ordering-table pointers g_2cc04/g_2cc08, primitive pool 0x2df40.
findings.interpretation: Consistent with C communal (uninitialized non-static) globals placed after all per-object .bss; their order is a linker decision that a natural link must reproduce. Boundary is approximate.
Candidate unit = handler + its init/step helpers; not proven (unreconstructed neighbours unknown).
Two readings: per-unit 4-byte .data in link order, or one unit declaring them consecutively. 0x128e0 being last despite early code favours the second.

findings: Index loops over a record table compile to a walking pointer biased to the first accessed field, with a signed compare against the biased end address. A pointer bound past a table therefore names the table, not the object that follows it.

Several region drafts named a record table by the first field they used, so one table appeared under several symbols. Before data closure, every array symbol needs an oracle check that no indexed access sits below it within one record stride.
fixes: Interior references to g_engine_interface fields replaced by the field (0x2bb44 context_004 in r1c430.c, 0x2bb54 data_014 in r19470.c); scripts/symbol_table.py now flags references inside the 1000-byte interface.

linker_probe.tool: python scripts/communal_probe.py (synthetic C objects, pinned RTM CL/LINK 5.00.7022, /OPT:NOREF)
rule: Initialized definitions (.data) come first, in object order.
Communal (tentatively defined, uninitialized non-static) variables are grouped by the first object in link order that defines them; extern references do not own.
Groups are emitted in reverse link order (the last object's communals first).
Within a group, variables follow that object's symbol order (observed: first-use order in its code); arrays larger than a word are aligned (0x20 observed).
linker_probe.title_check: TITLE shared .bss tail (>= ~0x2b370) shows grouping by subsystem (e.g. 0x2bf2c-0x2bffc for the object/sprite code 0x85b0-0x9300 and 0x17ad0; 0x2c144-0x2c160 for 0x6480/0x6670). Ordering against first-referencing function is inconclusive (21/57 descending violations vs 24/57 ascending) because owners are defining objects, which references cannot identify. Supports grouping; reverse order neither confirmed nor refuted.
linker_probe.cpp: A C++ object's namespace-scope `int x;` (extern "C") is an ordinary per-object .bss definition, never communal; C statics are per-object definitions too. Communals therefore come only from C units. Per-object .bss precedes all communals. TITLE's object-system tables at 0x2bf2c-0x2bffc lie in the shared tail and are read by C++-only functions, so they are probably defined (tentatively) in a C unit such as the one containing 0x17ad0.

resolved_conflicts.detail: Staged 0x5080 (r04d80.c) models the table as g_2cca8 with an id at +0; the 0x54f0 draft writes an index word at 0x2cca8+64k and dwords at 0x2cca0+64k, implying the record base is 0x2cca0 (index at +8). One object start must be chosen before data closure; the symbol check cannot see it without the object extent.
resolved_conflicts.resolution: Base is 0x2cca0: 24 records of 64 bytes. Every field reference lies in 0x00..0x3b from 0x2cca0. The loop bound 0x2d2a8 equals &g_2cca0[24].id_08, and with base 0x2cca8 the table would overlap the next referenced object 0x2d2a0 (32 x 4 bytes). Restaged r04d80.c with plain index loops over g_2cca0 (0x5080, 0x5a70, 0x5c60 masked equal); VC5 chooses the +8 walking pointer itself. The fake end symbols g_2d2a8 and g_2d2d0 (inside g_2d2a0) are gone, and unused interior declarations were removed. symbol_table.py now knows both table extents.

resolved_conflicts.detail: Three staged views used different bases: r04d80 g_26110 (state at +0x10), r04610 g_2611c (state at +4) with g_26134 and g_26288 as loop pointers, r18680 g_26114 (type at +0xc).
resolved_conflicts.resolution: Base is 0x26110: 18 records of 20 bytes. The original takes the record address with lea [i*20+0x26110], field references span +0x00..+0x13, loop bounds 0x2627c and 0x26288 are &g_26110[18] plus 4 and 0x10, and the next referenced object starts at 0x26278. r04610 (0x4b00 now a plain index loop) and r18680 were restaged with the same field offsets as r04d80, all masked equal. bss_order_rule.measured: Within one object, .bss order of C statics and C++ globals depends on the identifiers only: definition order and extra declarations do not change it, renaming one variable moves it.
bss_order_rule.falsified_models: additive, PJW, multiplicative (2..65599) and shift-xor hashes modulo 2..1099 and powers of two, on bare and underscore-decorated names (best 13/120 positions, chance level).
bss_order_rule.consequence: Reproducing a unit's .bss order needs the order function or names that satisfy it. The scheduler unit keeps 4 of its 6 variables at their original relative offsets. The others move, together with three 4-byte slots no code references (0x29e0c, 0x29e14, 0x29fa0), which are not invented.
bss_order_rule.controlled_probes: Single letters and two-letter names sort ascending regardless of definition order. For digit names the key behaves like h = h*4 + c taken modulo a table size, with equal keys putting the later-defined name first; each structured set fits exactly, but no table size fits a random-name set too (best 100/200 positions over shift/add/xor/rotate variants). Recovering the rule exactly would fix the .bss order of every unit; next lead: the compiler's symbol table code (read-only analysis), or more controlled probes (name length, character classes).

layout_blocker_L1.status: rule recovered 2026-10-09 (technical); applying it to names is a policy decision
layout_blocker_L1.rule: Within one object VC5 lays out file statics, C++ globals and C communals by ascending bucket of a 1024-entry identifier hash, later-defined name first within a bucket. h = (h >> 4) + 4*h + c over the identifier (the c1.dll interning hash, loop at 0x1060a47b); bucket = (h ^ (h >> 16)) & 0x3ff. scripts/symbol_order.py.
layout_blocker_L1.validation: Exact on 120 random names, 40 digit names, a 40-name mixed set (C statics), a 7-name C++ global set and a 14-variable C communal group; tests/test_symbol_order.py.
layout_blocker_L1.how_found: Names up to six characters sorted by h mod 1024; the 50 longer names fell inside the windows of their short neighbours only with the h ^ (h >> 16) fold.
layout_blocker_L1.consequence: In-object order is a pure function of the identifiers. The original order constrains the original names (bucket order along addresses); reproducing layout with chosen names awaits a project-owner decision on name policy.
